chunks: From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the bird has seized its wing, it belongs to the one who caught it."

key_terms.الطَّيْرُ: the bird, game (specifically birds in this context)
key_terms.مَلَكَ: to seize, to catch, to acquire possession

ai.seo_question: When does a hunter acquire ownership of the game during hunting?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *ghunm* (acquisition) in hunting, establishing that ownership is secured not merely by the initial strike but by the physical control or 'seizing' of the prey. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between a valid hunt and one that remains unclaimed, emphasizing the tangible transfer of possession. It reflects the practical legal standards of the early Islamic community regarding movable property and game rights.
